message.content:
Based on my search, here is a comprehensive overview of calcium-containing foods:

## Dairy Products (Highest Natural Sources)

Dairy products are among the most concentrated and well-absorbed sources of calcium:

- **Yogurt, plain low-fat** (8 oz): ~415 mg
- **Milk (nonfat/skim)** (1 cup): ~299-325 mg
- **Milk (whole)** (1 cup): ~276-300 mg
- **Mozzarella cheese, part-skim** (1.5 oz): ~333 mg
- **Cheddar cheese** (1.5 oz shredded): ~306 mg
- **Ricotta, part-skim** (1/2 cup): ~337 mg
- **Cottage cheese, 1% fat** (1 cup): ~138 mg

## Fish with Edible Bones

- **Sardines, canned in oil with bones** (3 oz): ~325 mg
- **Salmon, pink, canned with bones** (3 oz): ~181 mg

## Plant-Based Sources

### Leafy Green Vegetables
- **Collard greens, cooked** (1 cup): ~324 mg
- **Kale, cooked** (1 cup): ~94-177 mg
- **Bok choy (Chinese cabbage), cooked** (1 cup): ~158 mg
- **Turnip greens, boiled** (1/2 cup): ~99 mg
- **Broccoli, cooked** (1 cup): ~62-76 mg

*Note: Spinach is high in calcium but contains oxalic acid, which significantly reduces calcium absorption to only about 5%.*

### Legumes & Soy Products
- **Tofu, firm, made with calcium sulfate** (1/2 cup): ~253 mg; (1/4 block): up to 553 mg
- **Soybeans, cooked** (1/2 cup): ~131 mg
- **Edamame, cooked** (1 cup): ~130 mg
- **White beans/Navy beans, cooked** (1/2 cup): ~63-126 mg

### Nuts & Seeds
- **Chia seeds** (1 oz): ~179 mg
- **Sesame seeds** (3.5 oz/100g): ~670 mg
- **Almonds** (1 oz): ~76 mg
- **Tahini (sesame paste)** (1 tbsp): ~64 mg

### Other Plant Foods
- **Dried figs** (4): ~54 mg
- **Oranges** (1 medium): ~60-65 mg
- **Blackberries** (1 cup): ~42 mg

## Fortified Foods

Many foods are fortified with calcium, making them excellent sources:

- **Calcium-fortified orange juice** (1 cup): ~349 mg
- **Soy milk, fortified** (1 cup): ~299-399 mg
- **Almond milk, fortified** (1 cup): ~482 mg
- **Rice milk, fortified** (1 cup): ~300 mg
- **Breakfast cereals, fortified**: 100-1,000 mg per serving
- **Fortified instant cereals** (3.5 oz): up to 1,333 mg

## Other Sources

- **White bread** (3.5 oz): ~177 mg
- **Corn tortilla** (6" diameter): ~46 mg
- **Flour tortilla** (10"): ~90 mg

## Important Notes

- **Calcium absorption** from dairy and fortified foods is about 30%, while absorption from certain plants may be lower due to compounds like oxalic acid and phytic acid.
- Adults up to age 50 need about **1,000 mg/day**; women over 50 and men over 70 need **1,200 mg/day**.
- Vitamin D is essential for proper calcium absorption.

Sources:
1. https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Calcium-HealthProfessional/
2. https://www.health.harvard.edu/nutrition/calcium-rich-foods-how-to-boost-your-intake-of-this-important-mineral
3. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK45523/table/ch7.t2/
4. https://www.webmd.com/diet/foods-high-in-calcium
5. https://gp-training.hee.nhs.uk/windsor/wp-content/uploads/sites/96/2021/09/Vitamin-D-testing-and-treatment-guidelines.pdf
6. https://www.bucksformulary.nhs.uk/docs/Guideline_307FM.pdf
7. https://www.bucksformulary.nhs.uk/docs/Guideline_834FM.pdf?uid=598797444&uid2=2020111220184122
8. https://imsear.searo.who.int/bitstreams/99ce16a3-83a5-4fba-8f33-d0c9a0428303/download
